column1: # Duplicate endpoint pairs hidden behind a record-limit parameter - measured 2026-10-23
# lint_sources.check_dup_endpoint groups on host+path+QUERY, textually. A pair of
# rows that read ONE collection and differ only in how many records they ask for
# therefore never groups, so none of these is in lint_baseline.json. By that
# check's own reasoning they are real: uid = source_id|remote_key, so two sources
# on one endpoint store every record twice, in intel_items and in the FTS mirror,
# and spend two requests per cycle to do it.
# A record limit cannot select a different dataset, which is what makes this
# subclass decidable WITHOUT a live read - unlike the scope parameter that hid the
# IOC sea-level trio (showall=all / showall=a / absent), where only a fetch showed
# the server discards an unrecognised value and serves the default list.
# VERIFIED 2026-10-24 against the two false-positive mechanisms this list was
# published with a warning about. Re-harvested with C comments and .detail_url
# assignments stripped (a commented URL is documentation and is never fetched; a
# .detail_url is a per-record route, the {v} exclusion the lint already makes):
#   as harvested, the way lint_sources harvests   106 pairs
# The three that were documentation, not requests:
# The first attempt at this verification reported 0 surviving pairs, i.e. that
# every one was an artifact. That was wrong and the retraction would have been
# worse than the original claim: the line-comment regex `//[^\n]*` matches the
# `//` inside `https://`, so stripping deleted every URL in the tree -- 106,239
# of them -- and the check reported its own blindness as a clean result. Use
# `(?<!:)//[^\n]*`, and the script now refuses to print a number at all if
# stripping loses more than half the host+path groups. CLAUDE.md's rule earned
# again: zero findings from a new check deserves one suspicious look.
# STILL per-pair judgement before anything is retired. One distinction this
# list does NOT draw: a pair of two SCHEDULED rows duplicates a request on
# every cycle, whereas a pivot (entity token elsewhere in the URL) paired with
# a scheduled feed only double-STORES, since a pivot runs on demand. Both are
# rule-4b costs but they are not the same cost.
# kind. The repair is per-pair, as the 423 already in the baseline are.
# AND A LIMIT PAIR CAN BE DELIBERATE (osintsaas-43, 2026-10-24). Identical
# query strings do not mean identical purpose: two rows reading one collection
# at different limits may be an intentional pair, the way
# for the map, every observation for the series -- where the difference lives
# in the row's INTERVAL, record_type and page_resume, none of which appear in
# the URL this list groups on. Retiring either of those would be a real loss.
# This grouping requires every other query parameter to match, so a differing
# sort or filter already excludes a pair; what it cannot see is a difference
# declared in opts rather than in the query. Read the row, not just the URL.
# CLASSIFIED BY COST (2026-10-24), which is 43's distinction made countable:
#   BOTH_SCHEDULED   90   neither URL carries an entity token, so both rows run
#                         on a cadence -> a duplicated REQUEST every cycle on
#                         top of duplicated storage. Read these first.
#   BOTH_PIVOTS      13   both carry a token (e.g. gleif .../{qU}/...), so both
#                         run on demand -> duplicated storage, no duplicated
#   PIVOT_AND_FEED    0   see below -- this zero is an ARTIFACT, not a finding.
# The PIVOT_AND_FEED bucket cannot be populated by this method and its being
# empty says nothing about the tree. A token in the QUERY makes the two query
# strings differ by more than the limit, so the pair is excluded before it is
# classified; a token in the PATH is part of the host+path key, so both sides
# carry it and the pair lands in BOTH_PIVOTS. A pivot paired with a scheduled
# feed over one collection is therefore invisible HERE and still worth looking
# The token test is itself only a proxy -- the same proxy
# registry_is_entity_pivot() leans on. The authoritative test is interval == 0,
# which lives in the row's own declaration and not in its URL. So this ranks
# the list for reading; it decides nothing.
# replaces the token proxy above with each row's own `interval` and reads the
# fields the URL could not show. The counts move a long way once the rows are
# read instead of their URLs: 47 pairs are a generated feed row shadowing an
# hpengine row (the IOC shape), 33 are two generated rows over one endpoint,
# and only 13 are two hpengine rows - which is the one bucket where a
# deliberate pair can live. PIVOT_AND_FEED is 0 on the authoritative test too,
# though the grouping artifact described above still applies to it. Read that
# file before retiring anything; it also names the 8 pairs whose SURVIVING row
# has no id_keys, where retiring the generated side would leave rule 4b
# pairs: 103 verified of 106 harvested (90 both-scheduled, 13 both-pivots)
